semantic_contract: An instance method on Editors::cEditor that takes a three-valued mode selector and removes animated creatures from the editor, always returning nothing. With a null anim world at editor+0x360 every mode is a no-op. Mode 0 clears the attach flag at editor+0x385 through 0x0057e340 (only when the flag is currently set), then destroys the handle at editor+0x364 through Editors::cEditorAnimWorld::DestroyCreature and zeroes the field. Mode 2 does the same for editor+0x368 without touching the flag, and returns early if that handle is already null. Mode 1 works on the vector of 0x30-byte entries at editor+0x36c, whose element count is always the byte difference of the end and begin pointers divided by 0x30: when the second argument's low byte is non-zero it removes the LAST entry only, and when it is zero a zero third argument removes ALL entries while a non-zero third argument removes the FIRST entry whose dword 0 equals it, doing nothing when no entry matches. Every removal -- last, matched, or each of the clear-all pass -- performs the identical three-call sequence: an anim-world transform lookup of the entry's dword 0 into a 12-byte out block (0x0059d110), a notification on the singleton at 0x015d0c14 with key 0x03f1bf57, a zero selector and that block (0x0045af60), and then Editors::cEditorAnimWorld::DestroyCreature on the same dword 0. The entry is then unlinked: end -= 0x30 for the single-entry paths, a 0x30-stride shift-and-shrink (0x0057ef50) for the matched path, and a full zero-and-reset (0x009c69f0) for the clear-all path. No entry destructor ever runs, which is consistent with caller 0x0062ba10 clearing its own parallel index-keyed array immediately after the matched removal. Any mode other than 0, 1 or 2 does nothing, and modes 0 and 2 have no static call site anywhere in the binary.
classification_rationale: The complete 199-instruction body, the __thiscall ABI with three stack arguments and callee cleanup, every field offset, every constant, the whole branch polarity set and all three loops were read from the disassembly and corroborated by four disassembled callsites plus the sibling method Editors::cEditor::AddCreature at 0x00582fe0, whose three selector branches write to exactly the three destinations this function destroys, with the same 0x30 stride and the same notification key. All seven callees were read to their bodies. That rules out STRUCTURAL_ONLY and STILL_UNKNOWN. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because two material elements are bounded rather than established: (1) the owning class is INFERRED from the SDK address table's placement of AddCreature at 0x00582fe0 and nine other cEditor methods in the same region -- the binary has no MSVC RTTI and no cEditor vtable was located, so no class claim rests on a vtable; and (2) eleven of the twelve dwords of the 0x30-byte entry are never read by this function, and the notification key 0x03f1bf57 and the +0x385 attach flag have no established names.
semantic_findings: The function is the structural inverse of Editors::cEditor::AddCreature at 0x00582fe0: same three destinations, same 0x30 stride, same notification key.
The second argument is read as a byte, so only bit 0 of the pushed dword is observed; caller 0x0062c340 exploits that by pushing the same dword twice.
The element count is always (end - begin) / 48, computed by the MSVC 0x2aaaaaab idiom six times, and the caller 0x0062ba10 recomputes it independently with the same magic.
Element dword 0 is the anim-world handle, which AddCreature writes; the target passes it to both the transform lookup and DestroyCreature.
No element destructor runs on any path. The unlink is a bare pointer adjustment, and the caller clears its own parallel array afterwards.
Modes 0 and 2 have no static reference anywhere in the binary -- four xrefs, all calls, all from mode-1 callers -- so they are dead in this build unless reached by runtime patching.
Mode 0 clears the +0x385 attach flag before destroying the handle, and only when the flag is set; the setter 0x0057e340 writes that same offset itself.
The three-call detach protocol is duplicated verbatim three times in the listing, once for the last entry, once for the matched entry and once inside the clear-all loop.
0x00401050 does not pop its arguments: the three words pushed before it are consumed by 0x0045af60, which is why the pseudocode appears to give 0x00401050 three arguments.
The clear-all path runs the vector clear even when the vector is already empty, because the JLE at 0x00582f0a targets 0x00582f59, the instruction before the clear call.
Every path is idempotent: modes 0 and 2 are guarded on a null handle, mode 1 on an empty vector, and the matched removal returns without effect when nothing matches.
